text:
alex: Quick post — ran a 24h multi-tenant soak with the new kernel-selection path + the batching tweak and noticed steady KV memory growth for a subset of tenants. Not full leak, looks like slow page churn + fragmentation. Sharing logs and quick repro notes.

maria: thanks for flagging. can you paste the profile slices? which version did you run?

alex: ran on canary-2026-03-16 (kernel v3 heuristics). Attached sampled vmstats: `anon_rss` for worker-gpu-7 climbs ~120MB/day for tenant IDs A,B,C while others flat. Also saw increased pagewalks in perf: `page_faults: +18%`, `majflt: +2` (mostly soft).

chris: hm soft faults + fragmentation suggests inefficient slab reuse. any correlation with longctx requests?

alex: yes — tenants A/B have many longctx sessions ( > 32k tokens ) with repeated interleaved chats. KV cache hit rate for those tenants dips over time: 0.78 -> 0.63 across the run. eviction count also gradually rises.

sam: can you share the eviction policy + config used in the run?

alex: config snippet: ```
kv.eviction_policy: lru_segmented
kv.segment_size_kb: 512
kv.per_tenant_soft_quota_kb: 20480
kv.per_tenant_hard_quota_kb: 24576
kv.compaction_interval_s: 300
kv.page_walk_threshold: 512
```

maria: interesting. segmented LRU + compaction every 5m seems fine, but if longctx keeps creating large contiguous KV blobs we can get fragmentation that compaction doesn't fix quickly. Maybe compaction needs to be more aggressive for high-longctx tenants.

eng-bench: adding benchmark numbers: when we forced compaction every 30s for tenant A, steady-state KV residency stabilized and mem growth ceased, but CPU cost for compaction went up ~12%. tail-latency (p99) for generation increased by ~40ms.

chris: tradeoff as expected. We should consider per-tenant adaptive compaction: compaction frequency scales with longctx churn and fragmentation metric. Do we have a fragmentation counter?

alex: not currently exported. I instrumented a quick metric: `kv.fragmentation_ratio = (free_pages_in_segments / total_free_pages)` which hit 0.42 for tenant A at peak.

sam: propose a plan: 1) rollout fragmentation metric (prometheus) 2) add adaptive compaction rule: if frag_ratio > 0.3 and kv.hit_rate < 0.7 -> double compaction freq for the tenant 3) enforce soft quota eviction ramp earlier (soft_quota_pct -> 0.6) for noisy tenants 4) simulate + run 48h soak.

maria: +1. Also let's consider reclaim-by-reuse: when allocating segments we should prefer returning previously-freed contiguous ranges to same tenant to reduce cross-tenant fragmentation. That means adding a tenant-local freelist with coalescing.

chris: that will help cross-tenant fragmentation (noisy neighbor writes scattering free pages into global pool). Local freelist w/ coalescing is low-risk. We'll need metrics to detect whether freelist starvation causes more pagewalks.

eng-bench: did another run enabling tenant-local freelist in the allocator branch and leaving compaction at 5m. Results: tenant A memory plateaued, p50/p90 similar, CPU overhead negligible. We saw drop in pagewalks ~30%.

alex: nice. Any thoughts on quotas? Currently soft quota triggers only eviction of LRU pages but with longctx access pattern LRU evicts pages that will be hot again soon. That increases pagefault churn.

sam: we could implement recency-aware soft quota: protect N most-recent KV segments per tenant (or per-session) from eviction while applying eviction to older cold segments. Eg: protect the last 3 segments or 20% of tenant's resident pages.

maria: we should be careful: protecting too much increases starvation for others. Add a dynamic knob: protected_share = min(0.2, 0.5 * tenant_longctx_fraction). So only tenants with heavy longctx get slightly higher protection but bounded.

chris: also watching kernel selection regression: when we switched to new kernel path, its memory layout for KV nodes changed (extra 24 bytes per entry) — small but explains some base increase. We should roll a micro-optimization to pack flags and drop an unused pointer in node header.

alex: added an issue: "kv: compact kv_node header to save 24B/entry". Perf impact: saves ~3% memory for high-residency tenants.

sam: follow-up experiment plan pinned: - enable fragmentation metric + freelist in staging - run 48h multi-tenant soak with some tenants marked longctx-heavy - run two variants: (A) adaptive compaction + recency-protected soft quota (B) local freelist + baseline compaction - collect: mem growth curve, kv.hit_rate, pagewalks, p99 latency, compaction CPU cost - PRs: #4521 (freelist), #4523 (frag metric), #4525 (adaptive compaction)

maria: schedule a quick sync tomorrow 10:30 to triage results and pick which to canary. @chris please bring micro-profiling traces for kernel-node layout.

chris: will do. Also adding a small regression harness to assert no more than 100MB/day growth per tenant in soak.

runtime-bot: Deploy canary-2026-03-16 -> staging started by eng-bench at 2026-03-16T22:10:00Z :rocket:

alex: thanks all. I'll share raw logs + flamegraphs in the thread later (uploading now). cc @sam for quota knobs. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks. once we have frag metric in prod we can set alert: frag_ratio > 0.35 for 15m -> pagewalk spike and schedule auto-escalation to throttle tenant burst.

maria: agreed. also add a dashboard tile: per-tenant frag_ratio, per-tenant free_segments, per-tenant eviction_rate.

alex: uploaded flamegraph link: https://internal/redwood/fg/1796123456. I'll paste one snippet: `hot path: kv_lookup -> page_walk -> memcpy -> coalesce_free`

eng-bench: last note: in simulation we saw that tenants with interleaved many small sessions (chatty longctx) actually fragment less than tenants with a few extremely large sessions because allocations are more varied. So test mix matters.

maria: good point. include churn profiles in soak matrix.

chris: ok wrapping up. action items: alex instrument + upload raw metrics; eng-bench run planned variations; chris implement freelist coalescing PR; sam add quota knobs and alert thresholds. We'll reconvene after soak.

alex: solid. I'll open the metric PRs and tag everyone.

sam: :rocket:
